<pre>Regulation of ADMP and BMP2/4/7 at Opposite Embryonic Poles Generates a Self-Regulating Morphogenetic Field
Embryos have the ability to self-regulate and regenerate normal structures after being sectioned in half.
How is such a morphogenetic field established?
We discovered that quadruple knockdown of ADMP and BMP2/4/7 in Xenopus embryos eliminates self-regulation, causing ubiquitous neural induction throughout the ectoderm.
ADMP transcription in the Spemann organizer is activated at low BMP levels.
When ventral BMP2/4/7 signals are depleted, Admp expression increases, allowing for self-regulation.
ADMP has BMP-like activity and signals via the ALK-2 receptor.
It is unable to signal dorsally because of inhibition by Chordin.
The ventral BMP antagonists Sizzled and Bambi further refine the pattern.
By transplanting dorsal or ventral wild-type grafts into ADMP/BMP2/4/7-depleted hosts, we demonstrate that both poles serve as signaling centers that can induce histotypic differentiation over considerable distances.
We conclude that dorsal and ventral BMP signals and their extracellular antagonists expressed under opposing transcriptional regulation provide a molecular mechanism for embryonic self-regulation.</pre>

</details>

<details><summary>Rank 2 · 344523a580470c759c23e14d113e57e4 · document 14492964 · score 0.72679 · 170 tokens</summary>

<pre>The Spemann Organizer Signal noggin Binds and Inactivates Bone Morphogenetic Protein 4
Signals released by the Spemann organizer of the amphibian gastrula can directly induce neural tissue from ectoderm and can dorsalize ventral mesoderm to form muscle.
The secreted polypeptide noggin mimics these activities and is expressed at the appropriate time and place to participate in the organizer signal.
Neural induction and mesoderm dorsalization are antagonized by bone morphogenetic proteins (BMPs), which induce epidermis and ventral mesoderm instead.
Here we report that noggin protein binds BMP4 with high affinity and can abolish BMP4 activity by blocking binding to cognate cell-surface receptors.
These data suggest that noggin secreted by the organizer patterns the embryo by interrupting BMP signaling.</pre>

</details>

<details><summary>Rank 3 · 366f4a2258eceed687ef5ce871fe6a16 · document 1031534 · score 0.71581 · 252 tokens</summary>

<pre>Scaling of Dorsal-Ventral Patterning by Embryo Size-Dependent Degradation of Spemann’s Organizer Signals
Spemann&#x27;s organizer plays a key role in dorsal-ventral (DV) patterning in the amphibian embryo by secreting diffusible proteins such as Chordin, an antagonist to ventralizing bone morphogenetic proteins (BMPs).
The DV patterning is so robust that an amphibian embryo with its ventral half surgically removed can develop into a smaller but proportionally patterned larva.
Here, we show that this robust patterning depends on facilitated Chordin degradation and requires the expression of the Chordin-proteinase inhibitor Sizzled on the opposite side.
Sizzled, which is stable and diffuses widely along the DV axis, stabilizes Chordin and expands its distribution in the ventral direction.
This expanded Chordin distribution, in turn, limits BMP-dependent Sizzled production, forming an axis-wide feedback loop for shaping Chordin&#x27;s activity.
Using bisection assays, we demonstrate that Chordin degradation is dynamically controlled by embryo-size-coupled Sizzled accumulation.
We propose a scaling model that enables the DV pattern to adjust proportionally to embryonic axis size.</pre>

</details>

<details><summary>Rank 4 · 2be3b7dc6fe818970a8b7a0cc3a57f45 · document 23253955 · score 0.69109 · 280 tokens</summary>

<pre>Regulation of Pax-3 expression in the dermomyotome and its role in muscle development.
The segmented mesoderm in vertebrates gives rise to a variety of cell types in the embryo including the axial skeleton and muscle.
A number of transcription factors containing a paired domain (Pax proteins) are expressed in the segmented mesoderm during embryogenesis.
These include Pax-3 and a closely related gene, Pax-7, both of which are expressed in the segmental plate and in the dermomyotome.
In this paper, we show that signals from the notochord pattern the expression of Pax-3, Pax-7 and Pax-9 in somites and the subsequent differentiation of cell types that arise from the somitic mesoderm.
We directly assess the role of the Pax-3 gene in the differentiation of cell types derived from the dermomyotome by analyzing the development of muscle in splotch mouse embryos which lack a functional Pax-3 gene.
A population of Pax-3-expressing cells derived from the dermomyotome that normally migrate into the limb are absent in homozygous splotch embryos and, as a result, limb muscles are lost.
No abnormalities were detected in the trunk musculature of splotch embryos indicating that Pax-3 is necessary for the development of the limb but not trunk muscle.</pre>

</details>

<details><summary>Rank 5 · 5c2b8121a72e9174430d2497cac148c2 · document 5828251 · score 0.69046 · 336 tokens</summary>

<pre>Notch signalling acts in postmitotic avian myogenic cells to control MyoD activation.
During Drosophila myogenesis, Notch signalling acts at multiple steps of the muscle differentiation process.
In vertebrates, Notch activation has been shown to block MyoD activation and muscle differentiation in vitro, suggesting that this pathway may act to maintain the cells in an undifferentiated proliferative state.
In this paper, we address the role of Notch signalling in vivo during chick myogenesis.
We first demonstrate that the Notch1 receptor is expressed in postmitotic cells of the myotome and that the Notch ligands Delta1 and Serrate2 are detected in subsets of differentiating myogenic cells and are thus in position to signal to Notch1 during myogenic differentiation.
We also reinvestigate the expression of MyoD and Myf5 during avian myogenesis, and observe that Myf5 is expressed earlier than MyoD, consistent with previous results in the mouse.
We then show that forced expression of the Notch ligand, Delta1, during early myogenesis, using a retroviral system, has no effect on the expression of the early myogenic markers Pax3 and Myf5, but causes strong down-regulation of MyoD in infected somites.
Although Delta1 overexpression results in the complete lack of differentiated muscles, detailed examination of the infected embryos shows that initial formation of a myotome is not prevented, indicating that exit from the cell cycle has not been blocked.
These results suggest that Notch signalling acts in postmitotic myogenic cells to control a critical step of muscle differentiation.</pre>

</details>

<details><summary>Rank 6 · 704638493c12e4a309522ed487744229 · document 39763465 · score 0.68664 · 219 tokens</summary>

<pre>Combinatorial signaling by Sonic hedgehog and Wnt family members induces myogenic bHLH gene expression in the somite.
We have demonstrated previously that a combination of signals from the neural tube and the floor plate/notochord complex synergistically induce the expression of myogenic bHLH genes and myogenic differentiation markers in unspecified somites.
In this study we demonstrate that Sonic hedgehog (Shh), which is expressed in the floor plate/notochord, and a subset of Wnt family members (Wnt-1, Wnt-3, and Wnt-4), which are expressed in dorsal regions of the neural tube, mimic the muscle inducing activity of these tissues.
In combination, Shh and either Wnt-1 or Wnt-3 are sufficient to induce myogenesis in somitic tissue in vitro.
Therefore, we propose that myotome formation in vivo may be directed by the combinatorial activity of Shh secreted by ventral midline tissues (floor plate and notochord) and Wnt ligands secreted by the dorsal neural tube.</pre>

</details>

<details><summary>Rank 7 · deb12a411e8da4e6635a297d2f47aa2c · document 14296612 · score 0.68592 · 388 tokens</summary>

<pre>Dorsomorphin, a Selective Small Molecule Inhibitor of BMP Signaling, Promotes Cardiomyogenesis in Embryonic Stem Cells
BACKGROUND Pluripotent embryonic stem (ES) cells, which have the capacity to give rise to all tissue types in the body, show great promise as a versatile source of cells for regenerative therapy.
However, the basic mechanisms of lineage specification of pluripotent stem cells are largely unknown, and generating sufficient quantities of desired cell types remains a formidable challenge.
Small molecules, particularly those that modulate key developmental pathways like the bone morphogenetic protein (BMP) signaling cascade, hold promise as tools to study in vitro lineage specification and to direct differentiation of stem cells toward particular cell types.   

METHODOLOGY/ PRINCIPAL FINDINGS We describe the use of dorsomorphin, a selective small molecule inhibitor of BMP signaling, to induce myocardial differentiation in mouse ES cells.
Cardiac induction is very robust, increasing the yield of spontaneously beating cardiomyocytes by at least 20 fold.
Dorsomorphin, unlike the endogenous BMP antagonist Noggin, robustly induces cardiomyogenesis when treatment is limited to the initial 24-hours of ES cell differentiation.
Quantitative-PCR analyses of differentiating ES cells indicate that pharmacological inhibition of BMP signaling during the early critical stage promotes the development of the cardiomyocyte lineage, but reduces the differentiation of endothelial, smooth muscle, and hematopoietic cells.   

CONCLUSIONS/ SIGNIFICANCE Administration of a selective small molecule BMP inhibitor during the initial stages of ES cell differentiation substantially promotes the differentiation of primitive pluripotent cells toward the cardiomyocytic lineage, apparently at the expense of other mesodermal lineages.
Small molecule modulators of developmental pathways like dorsomorphin could become versatile pharmacological tools for stem cell research and regenerative medicine.</pre>

</details>

<details><summary>Rank 8 · 4a269a22c6c4b53ddb3d3c15b4dfacac · document 14105446 · score 0.68326 · 365 tokens</summary>

<pre>Inhibition of limb regeneration in the axolotl after treatment of the skin with actinomycin D.
In this experiment actinomycin D was used to explore the action of the wound epidermis on underlying tissues during limb regeneration.
In axolotl forelimbs the skin was removed from the elbow to the shoulder.
Skin from the right limbs was soaked for three hours in actinomycin D (5.0 or 10.0 μg/ml 0.6% NaCl).
For controls, skin from left limbs was soaked in 0.6% NaCl for the same period of time.
Each piece of skin was orthotopically replanted, and both limbs were amputated through the treated skin, proximal to the elbow.
After an initial healing period, the control limbs regenerated normally.
Except for a slightly paler color, limbs bearing actinomycin-treated skin were indistinguishable from the controls, both grossly and histologically, during the first week following amputation.
While the control limbs formed early blastemas, no grossly visible evidence of regeneration was apparent in the experimental limbs, but histologically some dedifferentiation was occurring.
Normally three to four digits were seen in the control regenerates before blastemas appeared on the experimental limbs.
By 35–40 days blastemas had appeared on most experimental limbs.
These developed very rapidly, and within a short time many of them had attained levels of development close to the controls.
Actinomycin D temporarily suppresses formation of the apical epidermal cap and the subsequent aggregation of dedifferentiated cells into a blastema.
When the effect wears off, an apical cap forms and the dedifferentiated cells quickly organize into a blastema and begin to differentiate.</pre>

</details>

<details><summary>Rank 9 · 2a3bd0d65fc4d8296105515162407ac2 · document 27569370 · score 0.67708 · 211 tokens</summary>

<pre>Emerging mechanisms in morphogen-mediated axon guidance.
Early in animal development, gradients of secreted morphogenic molecules, such as Sonic hedgehog (Shh), Wnt and TGFbeta/Bmp family members, regulate cell proliferation and determine the fate and phenotype of the target cells by activating well-characterized signalling pathways, which ultimately control gene transcription.
Shh, Wnt and TGFbeta/Bmp signalling also play an important and evolutionary conserved role in neural circuit assembly.
They regulate neuronal polarization, axon and dendrite development and synaptogenesis, processes that require rapid and local changes in cytoskeletal organization and plasma membrane components.
A key question then is whether morphogen signalling at the growth cone uses similar mechanisms and intracellular pathway components to those described for morphogen-mediated cell specification.
This review discusses recent advances towards the understanding of this problem, showing how Shh, Wnt and TGFbeta/Bmp have adapted their &#x27;classical&#x27; signalling pathways or adopted alternative and novel molecular mechanisms to influence different aspects of neuronal circuit formation.</pre>

</details>

<details><summary>Rank 10 · a6cfe1234925c8e8314e55e87e45ed63 · document 38380061 · score 0.67601 · 247 tokens</summary>

<pre>Localization and requirement for Myosin II at the dorsal-ventral compartment boundary of the Drosophila wing.
As organisms develop, their tissues can become separated into distinct cell populations through the establishment of compartment boundaries.
Compartment boundaries have been discovered in a wide variety of tissues, but in many cases the molecular mechanisms that separate cells remain poorly understood.
In the Drosophila wing, a stripe of Notch activation maintains the dorsal-ventral compartment boundary, through a process that depends on the actin cytoskeleton.
Here, we show that the dorsal-ventral boundary exhibits a distinct accumulation of Myosin II, and that this accumulation is regulated downstream of Notch signaling.
Conversely, the dorsal-ventral boundary is depleted for the Par-3 homologue Bazooka.
We further show that mutations in the Myosin heavy chain subunit encoded by zipper can impair dorsal-ventral compartmentalization without affecting anterior-posterior compartmentalization.
These observations identify a distinct accumulation and requirement for Myosin activity in dorsal-ventral compartmentalization, and suggest a novel mechanism in which contractile tension along an F-actin cable at the compartment boundary contributes to compartmentalization.</pre>

</details>

<pre>{
  &quot;selected_units&quot;: [
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;21f8d20647bb94286ac774361f4356ed&quot;,

      &quot;start&quot;: 105,
      &quot;end&quot;: 315,
      &quot;tokens&quot;: 51,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;Spemann&#x27;s organizer plays a key role in dorsal-ventral (DV) patterning in the amphibian embryo by secreting diffusible proteins such as Chordin, an antagonist to ventralizing bone morphogenetic proteins (BMPs).&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;5c7f28cb014f34d4cb6b0b2cda94d81f&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;366f4a2258eceed687ef5ce871fe6a16&quot;,
      &quot;document&quot;: &quot;1031534&quot;,
      &quot;kind&quot;: &quot;SENTENCE&quot;,
      &quot;start&quot;: 793,
      &quot;end&quot;: 945,
      &quot;tokens&quot;: 30,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;This expanded Chordin distribution, in turn, limits BMP-dependent Sizzled production, forming an axis-wide feedback loop for shaping Chordin&#x27;s activity.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;8331cb0b67287ef634cadb16f9db4d81&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;f4263525a6b0e458d98c7e682a769696&quot;,
      &quot;document&quot;: &quot;6076903&quot;,
      &quot;kind&quot;: &quot;SENTENCE&quot;,
      &quot;start&quot;: 261,
      &quot;end&quot;: 428,
      &quot;tokens&quot;: 36,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;We discovered that quadruple knockdown of ADMP and BMP2/4/7 in Xenopus embryos eliminates self-regulation, causing ubiquitous neural induction throughout the ectoderm.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;cc61664be799f340677e4a62d08d99b9&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;f4263525a6b0e458d98c7e682a769696&quot;,
      &quot;document&quot;: &quot;6076903&quot;,
      &quot;kind&quot;: &quot;SENTENCE&quot;,
      &quot;start&quot;: 669,
      &quot;end&quot;: 734,
      &quot;tokens&quot;: 14,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;It is unable to signal dorsally because of inhibition by Chordin.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;8e4ca0b533afa978d7abb4e578cfbebb&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;f4263525a6b0e458d98c7e682a769696&quot;,
      &quot;document&quot;: &quot;6076903&quot;,
      &quot;kind&quot;: &quot;SENTENCE&quot;,
      &quot;start&quot;: 809,
      &quot;end&quot;: 1025,
      &quot;tokens&quot;: 45,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;By transplanting dorsal or ventral wild-type grafts into ADMP/BMP2/4/7-depleted hosts, we demonstrate that both poles serve as signaling centers that can induce histotypic differentiation over considerable distances.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;43e84f4503fcf01f621a094ab12bb026&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;f4263525a6b0e458d98c7e682a769696&quot;,
      &quot;document&quot;: &quot;6076903&quot;,
      &quot;kind&quot;: &quot;SENTENCE&quot;,
      &quot;start&quot;: 1026,
      &quot;end&quot;: 1222,
      &quot;tokens&quot;: 32,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;We conclude that dorsal and ventral BMP signals and their extracellular antagonists expressed under opposing transcriptional regulation provide a molecular mechanism for embryonic self-regulation.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;733f9f9fb196cfd11c8c41e2fe1f6db4&quot;,

      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;Neural induction and mesoderm dorsalization are antagonized by bone morphogenetic proteins (BMPs), which induce epidermis and ventral mesoderm instead.&quot;
    }

<table><thead><tr><th>FIXED</th><th>QBGF</th><th>BEA_V1</th><th>BEA_V2</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><b>FIXED_SENTENCE</b><br>Score: 0.0000 (correctness)<br>Tokens: 1020/1024; unused: 4<br>Units: 27; parents: 9; FULL: 0<br>Stop: FROZEN_BASELINE<br>Answer:<pre>REFUTE</pre><details><summary>Exact saved reader context</summary><pre>Spemann&#x27;s organizer plays a key role in dorsal-ventral (DV) patterning in the amphibian embryo by secreting diffusible proteins such as Chordin, an antagonist to ventralizing bone morphogenetic proteins (BMPs).

Here, we show that this robust patterning depends on facilitated Chordin degradation and requires the expression of the Chordin-proteinase inhibitor Sizzled on the opposite side.

This expanded Chordin distribution, in turn, limits BMP-dependent Sizzled production, forming an axis-wide feedback loop for shaping Chordin&#x27;s activity.

In vertebrates, Notch activation has been shown to block MyoD activation and muscle differentiation in vitro, suggesting that this pathway may act to maintain the cells in an undifferentiated proliferative state.

Regulation of ADMP and BMP2/4/7 at Opposite Embryonic Poles Generates a Self-Regulating Morphogenetic Field

We discovered that quadruple knockdown of ADMP and BMP2/4/7 in Xenopus embryos eliminates self-regulation, causing ubiquitous neural induction throughout the ectoderm.

When ventral BMP2/4/7 signals are depleted, Admp expression increases, allowing for self-regulation.

It is unable to signal dorsally because of inhibition by Chordin.

By transplanting dorsal or ventral wild-type grafts into ADMP/BMP2/4/7-depleted hosts, we demonstrate that both poles serve as signaling centers that can induce histotypic differentiation over considerable distances.

We conclude that dorsal and ventral BMP signals and their extracellular antagonists expressed under opposing transcriptional regulation provide a molecular mechanism for embryonic self-regulation.

Dorsomorphin, a Selective Small Molecule Inhibitor of BMP Signaling, Promotes Cardiomyogenesis in Embryonic Stem Cells

METHODOLOGY/ PRINCIPAL FINDINGS We describe the use of dorsomorphin, a selective small molecule inhibitor of BMP signaling, to induce myocardial differentiation in mouse ES cells.

Dorsomorphin, unlike the endogenous BMP antagonist Noggin, robustly induces cardiomyogenesis when treatment is limited to the initial 24-hours of ES cell differentiation.

These include Pax-3 and a closely related gene, Pax-7, both of which are expressed in the segmental plate and in the dermomyotome.

In this paper, we show that signals from the notochord pattern the expression of Pax-3, Pax-7 and Pax-9 in somites and the subsequent differentiation of cell types that arise from the somitic mesoderm.

Early in animal development, gradients of secreted morphogenic molecules, such as Sonic hedgehog (Shh), Wnt and TGFbeta/Bmp family members, regulate cell proliferation and determine the fate and phenotype of the target cells by activating well-characterized signalling pathways, which ultimately control gene transcription.

In the Drosophila wing, a stripe of Notch activation maintains the dorsal-ventral compartment boundary, through a process that depends on the actin cytoskeleton.

Here, we show that the dorsal-ventral boundary exhibits a distinct accumulation of Myosin II, and that this accumulation is regulated downstream of Notch signaling.

We further show that mutations in the Myosin heavy chain subunit encoded by zipper can impair dorsal-ventral compartmentalization without affecting anterior-posterior compartmentalization.

These observations identify a distinct accumulation and requirement for Myosin activity in dorsal-ventral compartmentalization, and suggest a novel mechanism in which contractile tension along an F-actin cable at the compartment boundary contributes to compartmentalization.

We have demonstrated previously that a combination of signals from the neural tube and the floor plate/notochord complex synergistically induce the expression of myogenic bHLH genes and myogenic differentiation markers in unspecified somites.

In this study we demonstrate that Sonic hedgehog (Shh), which is expressed in the floor plate/notochord, and a subset of Wnt family members (Wnt-1, Wnt-3, and Wnt-4), which are expressed in dorsal regions of the neural tube, mimic the muscle inducing activity of these tissues.

Therefore, we propose that myotome formation in vivo may be directed by the combinatorial activity of Shh secreted by ventral midline tissues (floor plate and notochord) and Wnt ligands secreted by the dorsal neural tube.</pre></details></td><td><b>QBGF_FULL</b><br>Score: 0.0000 (correctness)<br>Tokens: 1015/1024; unused: 9<br>Units: 31; parents: 7; FULL: 0<br>Stop: FROZEN_BASELINE<br>Answer:<pre>REFUTE</pre><details><summary>Exact saved reader context</summary><pre>Spemann&#x27;s organizer plays a key role in dorsal-ventral (DV) patterning in the amphibian embryo by secreting diffusible proteins such as Chordin, an antagonist to ventralizing bone morphogenetic proteins (BMPs).

Here, we show that this robust patterning depends on facilitated Chordin degradation and requires the expression of the Chordin-proteinase inhibitor Sizzled on the opposite side.

Sizzled, which is stable and diffuses widely along the DV axis, stabilizes Chordin and expands its distribution in the ventral direction.

This expanded Chordin distribution, in turn, limits BMP-dependent Sizzled production, forming an axis-wide feedback loop for shaping Chordin&#x27;s activity.

Regulation of ADMP and BMP2/4/7 at Opposite Embryonic Poles Generates a Self-Regulating Morphogenetic Field

We discovered that quadruple knockdown of ADMP and BMP2/4/7 in Xenopus embryos eliminates self-regulation, causing ubiquitous neural induction throughout the ectoderm.

ADMP transcription in the Spemann organizer is activated at low BMP levels.

When ventral BMP2/4/7 signals are depleted, Admp expression increases, allowing for self-regulation.

ADMP has BMP-like activity and signals via the ALK-2 receptor.

It is unable to signal dorsally because of inhibition by Chordin.

By transplanting dorsal or ventral wild-type grafts into ADMP/BMP2/4/7-depleted hosts, we demonstrate that both poles serve as signaling centers that can induce histotypic differentiation over considerable distances.

We conclude that dorsal and ventral BMP signals and their extracellular antagonists expressed under opposing transcriptional regulation provide a molecular mechanism for embryonic self-regulation.

The Spemann Organizer Signal noggin Binds and Inactivates Bone Morphogenetic Protein 4

Signals released by the Spemann organizer of the amphibian gastrula can directly induce neural tissue from ectoderm and can dorsalize ventral mesoderm to form muscle.

The secreted polypeptide noggin mimics these activities and is expressed at the appropriate time and place to participate in the organizer signal.

Emerging mechanisms in morphogen-mediated axon guidance.

Early in animal development, gradients of secreted morphogenic molecules, such as Sonic hedgehog (Shh), Wnt and TGFbeta/Bmp family members, regulate cell proliferation and determine the fate and phenotype of the target cells by activating well-characterized signalling pathways, which ultimately control gene transcription.

Shh, Wnt and TGFbeta/Bmp signalling also play an important and evolutionary conserved role in neural circuit assembly.

They regulate neuronal polarization, axon and dendrite development and synaptogenesis, processes that require rapid and local changes in cytoskeletal organization and plasma membrane components.

A key question then is whether morphogen signalling at the growth cone uses similar mechanisms and intracellular pathway components to those described for morphogen-mediated cell specification.

This review discusses recent advances towards the understanding of this problem, showing how Shh, Wnt and TGFbeta/Bmp have adapted their &#x27;classical&#x27; signalling pathways or adopted alternative and novel molecular mechanisms to influence different aspects of neuronal circuit formation.

Here, we show that the dorsal-ventral boundary exhibits a distinct accumulation of Myosin II, and that this accumulation is regulated downstream of Notch signaling.

Combinatorial signaling by Sonic hedgehog and Wnt family members induces myogenic bHLH gene expression in the somite.

We have demonstrated previously that a combination of signals from the neural tube and the floor plate/notochord complex synergistically induce the expression of myogenic bHLH genes and myogenic differentiation markers in unspecified somites.

In this study we demonstrate that Sonic hedgehog (Shh), which is expressed in the floor plate/notochord, and a subset of Wnt family members (Wnt-1, Wnt-3, and Wnt-4), which are expressed in dorsal regions of the neural tube, mimic the muscle inducing activity of these tissues.

In combination, Shh and either Wnt-1 or Wnt-3 are sufficient to induce myogenesis in somitic tissue in vitro.

Therefore, we propose that myotome formation in vivo may be directed by the combinatorial activity of Shh secreted by ventral midline tissues (floor plate and notochord) and Wnt ligands secreted by the dorsal neural tube.</pre></details></td><td><b>BEA_QBGF_V1</b><br>Score: 1.0000 (correctness)<br>Tokens: 561/1024; unused: 463<br>Units: 27; parents: 10; FULL: 0<br>Stop: LOW_MARGINAL_VALUE<br>Answer:<pre>NOT_ENOUGH_INFO</pre><details><summary>Exact saved reader context</summary><pre>This expanded Chordin distribution, in turn, limits BMP-dependent Sizzled production, forming an axis-wide feedback loop for shaping Chordin&#x27;s activity.

      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;8331cb0b67287ef634cadb16f9db4d81&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;f4263525a6b0e458d98c7e682a769696&quot;,
      &quot;document&quot;: &quot;6076903&quot;,
      &quot;kind&quot;: &quot;SENTENCE&quot;,
      &quot;start&quot;: 261,
      &quot;end&quot;: 428,
      &quot;tokens&quot;: 36,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;We discovered that quadruple knockdown of ADMP and BMP2/4/7 in Xenopus embryos eliminates self-regulation, causing ubiquitous neural induction throughout the ectoderm.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;1023e18cbc4e3d8d58491e5cead9b0f6&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;f4263525a6b0e458d98c7e682a769696&quot;,
      &quot;document&quot;: &quot;6076903&quot;,
      &quot;kind&quot;: &quot;SENTENCE&quot;,
      &quot;start&quot;: 505,
      &quot;end&quot;: 605,
      &quot;tokens&quot;: 24,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;When ventral BMP2/4/7 signals are depleted, Admp expression increases, allowing for self-regulation.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;cc61664be799f340677e4a62d08d99b9&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;f4263525a6b0e458d98c7e682a769696&quot;,
      &quot;document&quot;: &quot;6076903&quot;,
      &quot;kind&quot;: &quot;SENTENCE&quot;,
      &quot;start&quot;: 669,
      &quot;end&quot;: 734,
      &quot;tokens&quot;: 14,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;It is unable to signal dorsally because of inhibition by Chordin.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;8e4ca0b533afa978d7abb4e578cfbebb&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;f4263525a6b0e458d98c7e682a769696&quot;,
      &quot;document&quot;: &quot;6076903&quot;,
      &quot;kind&quot;: &quot;SENTENCE&quot;,
      &quot;start&quot;: 809,
      &quot;end&quot;: 1025,
      &quot;tokens&quot;: 45,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;By transplanting dorsal or ventral wild-type grafts into ADMP/BMP2/4/7-depleted hosts, we demonstrate that both poles serve as signaling centers that can induce histotypic differentiation over considerable distances.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;43e84f4503fcf01f621a094ab12bb026&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;f4263525a6b0e458d98c7e682a769696&quot;,
      &quot;document&quot;: &quot;6076903&quot;,
      &quot;kind&quot;: &quot;SENTENCE&quot;,
      &quot;start&quot;: 1026,
      &quot;end&quot;: 1222,
      &quot;tokens&quot;: 32,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;We conclude that dorsal and ventral BMP signals and their extracellular antagonists expressed under opposing transcriptional regulation provide a molecular mechanism for embryonic self-regulation.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;ae266fd30355fe786d72f3d633bb4f9d&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;deb12a411e8da4e6635a297d2f47aa2c&quot;,
      &quot;document&quot;: &quot;14296612&quot;,
      &quot;kind&quot;: &quot;SENTENCE&quot;,
      &quot;start&quot;: 0,
      &quot;end&quot;: 118,
      &quot;tokens&quot;: 32,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;Dorsomorphin, a Selective Small Molecule Inhibitor of BMP Signaling, Promotes Cardiomyogenesis in Embryonic Stem Cells&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;8c5849a3113f95a77a26527d666bdb3b&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;deb12a411e8da4e6635a297d2f47aa2c&quot;,
      &quot;document&quot;: &quot;14296612&quot;,
      &quot;kind&quot;: &quot;SENTENCE&quot;,
      &quot;start&quot;: 786,
      &quot;end&quot;: 965,
      &quot;tokens&quot;: 40,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;METHODOLOGY/ PRINCIPAL FINDINGS We describe the use of dorsomorphin, a selective small molecule inhibitor of BMP signaling, to induce myocardial differentiation in mouse ES cells.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;68dfcc7fae179b797d0b318f149c816c&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;deb12a411e8da4e6635a297d2f47aa2c&quot;,
      &quot;document&quot;: &quot;14296612&quot;,
      &quot;kind&quot;: &quot;SENTENCE&quot;,
      &quot;start&quot;: 1082,
      &quot;end&quot;: 1252,
      &quot;tokens&quot;: 38,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;Dorsomorphin, unlike the endogenous BMP antagonist Noggin, robustly induces cardiomyogenesis when treatment is limited to the initial 24-hours of ES cell differentiation.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;40ac0b8144e86dbc1518234c2b4ec04f&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;344523a580470c759c23e14d113e57e4&quot;,
      &quot;document&quot;: &quot;14492964&quot;,
      &quot;kind&quot;: &quot;SENTENCE&quot;,
      &quot;start&quot;: 0,
      &quot;end&quot;: 86,
      &quot;tokens&quot;: 20,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;The Spemann Organizer Signal noggin Binds and Inactivates Bone Morphogenetic Protein 4&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;38cfcaa033ecca4af55fe4cd176bf919&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;344523a580470c759c23e14d113e57e4&quot;,
      &quot;document&quot;: &quot;14492964&quot;,
      &quot;kind&quot;: &quot;SENTENCE&quot;,
      &quot;start&quot;: 254,
      &quot;end&quot;: 400,
      &quot;tokens&quot;: 28,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;The secreted polypeptide noggin mimics these activities and is expressed at the appropriate time and place to participate in the organizer signal.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;733f9f9fb196cfd11c8c41e2fe1f6db4&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;344523a580470c759c23e14d113e57e4&quot;,
      &quot;document&quot;: &quot;14492964&quot;,
      &quot;kind&quot;: &quot;SENTENCE&quot;,
      &quot;start&quot;: 401,
      &quot;end&quot;: 552,
      &quot;tokens&quot;: 36,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;Neural induction and mesoderm dorsalization are antagonized by bone morphogenetic proteins (BMPs), which induce epidermis and ventral mesoderm instead.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;8f0cd0dc365ffb28c1e801ad4f0afdcd&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;2be3b7dc6fe818970a8b7a0cc3a57f45&quot;,
      &quot;document&quot;: &quot;23253955&quot;,
      &quot;kind&quot;: &quot;SENTENCE&quot;,
      &quot;start&quot;: 218,
      &quot;end&quot;: 355,
      &quot;tokens&quot;: 26,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;A number of transcription factors containing a paired domain (Pax proteins) are expressed in the segmented mesoderm during embryogenesis.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;cb251f4e015702d5e8f37abf511e80bc&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;2be3b7dc6fe818970a8b7a0cc3a57f45&quot;,
      &quot;document&quot;: &quot;23253955&quot;,
      &quot;kind&quot;: &quot;SENTENCE&quot;,
      &quot;start&quot;: 356,
      &quot;end&quot;: 486,
      &quot;tokens&quot;: 34,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;These include Pax-3 and a closely related gene, Pax-7, both of which are expressed in the segmental plate and in the dermomyotome.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;567317878b1a6be303ea116926dfc797&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;2be3b7dc6fe818970a8b7a0cc3a57f45&quot;,
      &quot;document&quot;: &quot;23253955&quot;,
      &quot;kind&quot;: &quot;SENTENCE&quot;,
      &quot;start&quot;: 487,
      &quot;end&quot;: 688,
      &quot;tokens&quot;: 48,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;In this paper, we show that signals from the notochord pattern the expression of Pax-3, Pax-7 and Pax-9 in somites and the subsequent differentiation of cell types that arise from the somitic mesoderm.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;148e798552d705ba6fae2ff15af08d68&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;2a3bd0d65fc4d8296105515162407ac2&quot;,
      &quot;document&quot;: &quot;27569370&quot;,
      &quot;kind&quot;: &quot;SENTENCE&quot;,
      &quot;start&quot;: 57,
      &quot;end&quot;: 380,
      &quot;tokens&quot;: 60,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;Early in animal development, gradients of secreted morphogenic molecules, such as Sonic hedgehog (Shh), Wnt and TGFbeta/Bmp family members, regulate cell proliferation and determine the fate and phenotype of the target cells by activating well-characterized signalling pathways, which ultimately control gene transcription.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;4cfd460a6cd2393122de4934c4b071b7&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;a6cfe1234925c8e8314e55e87e45ed63&quot;,
      &quot;document&quot;: &quot;38380061&quot;,
      &quot;kind&quot;: &quot;SENTENCE&quot;,
      &quot;start&quot;: 414,
      &quot;end&quot;: 575,
      &quot;tokens&quot;: 36,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;In the Drosophila wing, a stripe of Notch activation maintains the dorsal-ventral compartment boundary, through a process that depends on the actin cytoskeleton.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;6f83589d9448236c50dff567bac57407&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;a6cfe1234925c8e8314e55e87e45ed63&quot;,
      &quot;document&quot;: &quot;38380061&quot;,
      &quot;kind&quot;: &quot;SENTENCE&quot;,
      &quot;start&quot;: 576,
      &quot;end&quot;: 740,
      &quot;tokens&quot;: 33,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;Here, we show that the dorsal-ventral boundary exhibits a distinct accumulation of Myosin II, and that this accumulation is regulated downstream of Notch signaling.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;d40df1c7434094f5f63ccad851c84f07&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;a6cfe1234925c8e8314e55e87e45ed63&quot;,
      &quot;document&quot;: &quot;38380061&quot;,
      &quot;kind&quot;: &quot;SENTENCE&quot;,
      &quot;start&quot;: 826,
      &quot;end&quot;: 1014,
      &quot;tokens&quot;: 35,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;We further show that mutations in the Myosin heavy chain subunit encoded by zipper can impair dorsal-ventral compartmentalization without affecting anterior-posterior compartmentalization.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;75f1b77287230a31b7962ca60e400f2d&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;a6cfe1234925c8e8314e55e87e45ed63&quot;,
      &quot;document&quot;: &quot;38380061&quot;,
      &quot;kind&quot;: &quot;SENTENCE&quot;,
      &quot;start&quot;: 1015,
      &quot;end&quot;: 1289,
      &quot;tokens&quot;: 49,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;These observations identify a distinct accumulation and requirement for Myosin activity in dorsal-ventral compartmentalization, and suggest a novel mechanism in which contractile tension along an F-actin cable at the compartment boundary contributes to compartmentalization.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;0a7e8081a354440f36a34d902fcdbd66&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;704638493c12e4a309522ed487744229&quot;,
      &quot;document&quot;: &quot;39763465&quot;,
      &quot;kind&quot;: &quot;SENTENCE&quot;,
      &quot;start&quot;: 118,
      &quot;end&quot;: 360,
      &quot;tokens&quot;: 43,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;We have demonstrated previously that a combination of signals from the neural tube and the floor plate/notochord complex synergistically induce the expression of myogenic bHLH genes and myogenic differentiation markers in unspecified somites.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;2726f0a4d4dc4a2ceae6f2d4415554bc&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;704638493c12e4a309522ed487744229&quot;,
      &quot;document&quot;: &quot;39763465&quot;,
      &quot;kind&quot;: &quot;SENTENCE&quot;,
      &quot;start&quot;: 361,
      &quot;end&quot;: 638,
      &quot;tokens&quot;: 69,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;In this study we demonstrate that Sonic hedgehog (Shh), which is expressed in the floor plate/notochord, and a subset of Wnt family members (Wnt-1, Wnt-3, and Wnt-4), which are expressed in dorsal regions of the neural tube, mimic the muscle inducing activity of these tissues.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;0f572e2820ef9d83c4678562c93e7b9e&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;704638493c12e4a309522ed487744229&quot;,
      &quot;document&quot;: &quot;39763465&quot;,
      &quot;kind&quot;: &quot;SENTENCE&quot;,
      &quot;start&quot;: 749,
      &quot;end&quot;: 970,
      &quot;tokens&quot;: 52,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;Therefore, we propose that myotome formation in vivo may be directed by the combinatorial activity of Shh secreted by ventral midline tissues (floor plate and notochord) and Wnt ligands secreted by the dorsal neural tube.&quot;
    }
  ],

<pre>{
  &quot;selected_units&quot;: [
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;21f8d20647bb94286ac774361f4356ed&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;366f4a2258eceed687ef5ce871fe6a16&quot;,

      &quot;kind&quot;: &quot;SENTENCE&quot;,
      &quot;start&quot;: 105,
      &quot;end&quot;: 315,
      &quot;tokens&quot;: 51,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;Spemann&#x27;s organizer plays a key role in dorsal-ventral (DV) patterning in the amphibian embryo by secreting diffusible proteins such as Chordin, an antagonist to ventralizing bone morphogenetic proteins (BMPs).&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;1a83969da35277b2ac7caec4e7afb37d&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;366f4a2258eceed687ef5ce871fe6a16&quot;,
      &quot;document&quot;: &quot;1031534&quot;,
      &quot;kind&quot;: &quot;SENTENCE&quot;,
      &quot;start&quot;: 476,
      &quot;end&quot;: 654,
      &quot;tokens&quot;: 35,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;Here, we show that this robust patterning depends on facilitated Chordin degradation and requires the expression of the Chordin-proteinase inhibitor Sizzled on the opposite side.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;61c62ce50e266d90aff080eee73aa037&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;366f4a2258eceed687ef5ce871fe6a16&quot;,
      &quot;document&quot;: &quot;1031534&quot;,
      &quot;kind&quot;: &quot;SENTENCE&quot;,
      &quot;start&quot;: 655,
      &quot;end&quot;: 792,
      &quot;tokens&quot;: 30,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;Sizzled, which is stable and diffuses widely along the DV axis, stabilizes Chordin and expands its distribution in the ventral direction.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;5c7f28cb014f34d4cb6b0b2cda94d81f&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;366f4a2258eceed687ef5ce871fe6a16&quot;,
      &quot;document&quot;: &quot;1031534&quot;,
      &quot;kind&quot;: &quot;SENTENCE&quot;,
      &quot;start&quot;: 793,
      &quot;end&quot;: 945,
      &quot;tokens&quot;: 30,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;This expanded Chordin distribution, in turn, limits BMP-dependent Sizzled production, forming an axis-wide feedback loop for shaping Chordin&#x27;s activity.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;a88e5db2d5a1d40c1b264869fcf7014d&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;f4263525a6b0e458d98c7e682a769696&quot;,
      &quot;document&quot;: &quot;6076903&quot;,
      &quot;kind&quot;: &quot;SENTENCE&quot;,
      &quot;start&quot;: 0,
      &quot;end&quot;: 107,
      &quot;tokens&quot;: 30,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;Regulation of ADMP and BMP2/4/7 at Opposite Embryonic Poles Generates a Self-Regulating Morphogenetic Field&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;8331cb0b67287ef634cadb16f9db4d81&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;f4263525a6b0e458d98c7e682a769696&quot;,
      &quot;document&quot;: &quot;6076903&quot;,
      &quot;kind&quot;: &quot;SENTENCE&quot;,
      &quot;start&quot;: 261,
      &quot;end&quot;: 428,
      &quot;tokens&quot;: 36,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;We discovered that quadruple knockdown of ADMP and BMP2/4/7 in Xenopus embryos eliminates self-regulation, causing ubiquitous neural induction throughout the ectoderm.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;2f88107ef152ada1e4c7e6cc723d5c27&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;f4263525a6b0e458d98c7e682a769696&quot;,
      &quot;document&quot;: &quot;6076903&quot;,
      &quot;kind&quot;: &quot;SENTENCE&quot;,
      &quot;start&quot;: 429,
      &quot;end&quot;: 504,
      &quot;tokens&quot;: 15,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;ADMP transcription in the Spemann organizer is activated at low BMP levels.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;1023e18cbc4e3d8d58491e5cead9b0f6&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;f4263525a6b0e458d98c7e682a769696&quot;,
      &quot;document&quot;: &quot;6076903&quot;,
      &quot;kind&quot;: &quot;SENTENCE&quot;,
      &quot;start&quot;: 505,
      &quot;end&quot;: 605,
      &quot;tokens&quot;: 24,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;When ventral BMP2/4/7 signals are depleted, Admp expression increases, allowing for self-regulation.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;a93c3348c775b02c8372c579f3a8ba1b&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;f4263525a6b0e458d98c7e682a769696&quot;,
      &quot;document&quot;: &quot;6076903&quot;,
      &quot;kind&quot;: &quot;SENTENCE&quot;,
      &quot;start&quot;: 606,
      &quot;end&quot;: 668,
      &quot;tokens&quot;: 16,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;ADMP has BMP-like activity and signals via the ALK-2 receptor.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;cc61664be799f340677e4a62d08d99b9&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;f4263525a6b0e458d98c7e682a769696&quot;,
      &quot;document&quot;: &quot;6076903&quot;,
      &quot;kind&quot;: &quot;SENTENCE&quot;,
      &quot;start&quot;: 669,
      &quot;end&quot;: 734,
      &quot;tokens&quot;: 14,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;It is unable to signal dorsally because of inhibition by Chordin.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;8e4ca0b533afa978d7abb4e578cfbebb&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;f4263525a6b0e458d98c7e682a769696&quot;,
      &quot;document&quot;: &quot;6076903&quot;,
      &quot;kind&quot;: &quot;SENTENCE&quot;,
      &quot;start&quot;: 809,
      &quot;end&quot;: 1025,
      &quot;tokens&quot;: 45,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;By transplanting dorsal or ventral wild-type grafts into ADMP/BMP2/4/7-depleted hosts, we demonstrate that both poles serve as signaling centers that can induce histotypic differentiation over considerable distances.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;43e84f4503fcf01f621a094ab12bb026&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;f4263525a6b0e458d98c7e682a769696&quot;,
      &quot;document&quot;: &quot;6076903&quot;,
      &quot;kind&quot;: &quot;SENTENCE&quot;,
      &quot;start&quot;: 1026,
      &quot;end&quot;: 1222,
      &quot;tokens&quot;: 32,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;We conclude that dorsal and ventral BMP signals and their extracellular antagonists expressed under opposing transcriptional regulation provide a molecular mechanism for embryonic self-regulation.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;b5e12ba3a018a7670e195c5cde04a9b5&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;4a269a22c6c4b53ddb3d3c15b4dfacac&quot;,
      &quot;document&quot;: &quot;14105446&quot;,
      &quot;kind&quot;: &quot;SENTENCE&quot;,
      &quot;start&quot;: 0,
      &quot;end&quot;: 94,
      &quot;tokens&quot;: 23,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;Inhibition of limb regeneration in the axolotl after treatment of the skin with actinomycin D.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;40ac0b8144e86dbc1518234c2b4ec04f&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;344523a580470c759c23e14d113e57e4&quot;,
      &quot;document&quot;: &quot;14492964&quot;,
      &quot;kind&quot;: &quot;SENTENCE&quot;,
      &quot;start&quot;: 0,
      &quot;end&quot;: 86,
      &quot;tokens&quot;: 20,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;The Spemann Organizer Signal noggin Binds and Inactivates Bone Morphogenetic Protein 4&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;198f4196a5b7fdc378cb9e3b8a7db80b&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;344523a580470c759c23e14d113e57e4&quot;,
      &quot;document&quot;: &quot;14492964&quot;,
      &quot;kind&quot;: &quot;SENTENCE&quot;,
      &quot;start&quot;: 87,
      &quot;end&quot;: 253,
      &quot;tokens&quot;: 35,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;Signals released by the Spemann organizer of the amphibian gastrula can directly induce neural tissue from ectoderm and can dorsalize ventral mesoderm to form muscle.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;38cfcaa033ecca4af55fe4cd176bf919&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;344523a580470c759c23e14d113e57e4&quot;,
      &quot;document&quot;: &quot;14492964&quot;,
      &quot;kind&quot;: &quot;SENTENCE&quot;,
      &quot;start&quot;: 254,
      &quot;end&quot;: 400,
      &quot;tokens&quot;: 28,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;The secreted polypeptide noggin mimics these activities and is expressed at the appropriate time and place to participate in the organizer signal.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;733f9f9fb196cfd11c8c41e2fe1f6db4&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;344523a580470c759c23e14d113e57e4&quot;,
      &quot;document&quot;: &quot;14492964&quot;,
      &quot;kind&quot;: &quot;SENTENCE&quot;,
      &quot;start&quot;: 401,
      &quot;end&quot;: 552,
      &quot;tokens&quot;: 36,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;Neural induction and mesoderm dorsalization are antagonized by bone morphogenetic proteins (BMPs), which induce epidermis and ventral mesoderm instead.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;487bc09fea5ef6f793f17a62254509c4&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;344523a580470c759c23e14d113e57e4&quot;,
      &quot;document&quot;: &quot;14492964&quot;,
      &quot;kind&quot;: &quot;SENTENCE&quot;,
      &quot;start&quot;: 553,
      &quot;end&quot;: 702,
      &quot;tokens&quot;: 30,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;Here we report that noggin protein binds BMP4 with high affinity and can abolish BMP4 activity by blocking binding to cognate cell-surface receptors.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;0ebd7f1ca1d43f282177e76a57c4006e&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;344523a580470c759c23e14d113e57e4&quot;,
      &quot;document&quot;: &quot;14492964&quot;,
      &quot;kind&quot;: &quot;SENTENCE&quot;,
      &quot;start&quot;: 703,
      &quot;end&quot;: 810,
      &quot;tokens&quot;: 20,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;These data suggest that noggin secreted by the organizer patterns the embryo by interrupting BMP signaling.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;944d0d2141a1f33d96065b79ab6a8453&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;2a3bd0d65fc4d8296105515162407ac2&quot;,
      &quot;document&quot;: &quot;27569370&quot;,
      &quot;kind&quot;: &quot;SENTENCE&quot;,
      &quot;start&quot;: 0,
      &quot;end&quot;: 56,
      &quot;tokens&quot;: 11,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;Emerging mechanisms in morphogen-mediated axon guidance.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;148e798552d705ba6fae2ff15af08d68&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;2a3bd0d65fc4d8296105515162407ac2&quot;,
      &quot;document&quot;: &quot;27569370&quot;,
      &quot;kind&quot;: &quot;SENTENCE&quot;,
      &quot;start&quot;: 57,
      &quot;end&quot;: 380,
      &quot;tokens&quot;: 60,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;Early in animal development, gradients of secreted morphogenic molecules, such as Sonic hedgehog (Shh), Wnt and TGFbeta/Bmp family members, regulate cell proliferation and determine the fate and phenotype of the target cells by activating well-characterized signalling pathways, which ultimately control gene transcription.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;65f1149258c9df30c00a1335519ac323&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;2a3bd0d65fc4d8296105515162407ac2&quot;,
      &quot;document&quot;: &quot;27569370&quot;,
      &quot;kind&quot;: &quot;SENTENCE&quot;,
      &quot;start&quot;: 381,
      &quot;end&quot;: 499,
      &quot;tokens&quot;: 26,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;Shh, Wnt and TGFbeta/Bmp signalling also play an important and evolutionary conserved role in neural circuit assembly.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;902f2d36b38349381625d6d3ece61ff5&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;2a3bd0d65fc4d8296105515162407ac2&quot;,
      &quot;document&quot;: &quot;27569370&quot;,
      &quot;kind&quot;: &quot;SENTENCE&quot;,
      &quot;start&quot;: 500,
      &quot;end&quot;: 694,
      &quot;tokens&quot;: 33,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;They regulate neuronal polarization, axon and dendrite development and synaptogenesis, processes that require rapid and local changes in cytoskeletal organization and plasma membrane components.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;1292419e558246c9f1a488979b7b2b2f&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;2a3bd0d65fc4d8296105515162407ac2&quot;,
      &quot;document&quot;: &quot;27569370&quot;,
      &quot;kind&quot;: &quot;SENTENCE&quot;,
      &quot;start&quot;: 695,
      &quot;end&quot;: 888,
      &quot;tokens&quot;: 31,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;A key question then is whether morphogen signalling at the growth cone uses similar mechanisms and intracellular pathway components to those described for morphogen-mediated cell specification.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;8c8a7dc7d49c5c04221b6cea6fe2a2cd&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;2a3bd0d65fc4d8296105515162407ac2&quot;,
      &quot;document&quot;: &quot;27569370&quot;,
      &quot;kind&quot;: &quot;SENTENCE&quot;,
      &quot;start&quot;: 889,
      &quot;end&quot;: 1173,
      &quot;tokens&quot;: 50,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;This review discusses recent advances towards the understanding of this problem, showing how Shh, Wnt and TGFbeta/Bmp have adapted their &#x27;classical&#x27; signalling pathways or adopted alternative and novel molecular mechanisms to influence different aspects of neuronal circuit formation.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;6f83589d9448236c50dff567bac57407&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;a6cfe1234925c8e8314e55e87e45ed63&quot;,
      &quot;document&quot;: &quot;38380061&quot;,
      &quot;kind&quot;: &quot;SENTENCE&quot;,
      &quot;start&quot;: 576,
      &quot;end&quot;: 740,
      &quot;tokens&quot;: 33,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;Here, we show that the dorsal-ventral boundary exhibits a distinct accumulation of Myosin II, and that this accumulation is regulated downstream of Notch signaling.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;d751468a66e439fd522da43ce8f33a50&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;704638493c12e4a309522ed487744229&quot;,
      &quot;document&quot;: &quot;39763465&quot;,
      &quot;kind&quot;: &quot;SENTENCE&quot;,
      &quot;start&quot;: 0,
      &quot;end&quot;: 117,
      &quot;tokens&quot;: 26,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;Combinatorial signaling by Sonic hedgehog and Wnt family members induces myogenic bHLH gene expression in the somite.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;0a7e8081a354440f36a34d902fcdbd66&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;704638493c12e4a309522ed487744229&quot;,
      &quot;document&quot;: &quot;39763465&quot;,
      &quot;kind&quot;: &quot;SENTENCE&quot;,
      &quot;start&quot;: 118,
      &quot;end&quot;: 360,
      &quot;tokens&quot;: 43,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;We have demonstrated previously that a combination of signals from the neural tube and the floor plate/notochord complex synergistically induce the expression of myogenic bHLH genes and myogenic differentiation markers in unspecified somites.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;2726f0a4d4dc4a2ceae6f2d4415554bc&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;704638493c12e4a309522ed487744229&quot;,
      &quot;document&quot;: &quot;39763465&quot;,
      &quot;kind&quot;: &quot;SENTENCE&quot;,
      &quot;start&quot;: 361,
      &quot;end&quot;: 638,
      &quot;tokens&quot;: 69,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;In this study we demonstrate that Sonic hedgehog (Shh), which is expressed in the floor plate/notochord, and a subset of Wnt family members (Wnt-1, Wnt-3, and Wnt-4), which are expressed in dorsal regions of the neural tube, mimic the muscle inducing activity of these tissues.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;ef356c352e1668673a5f2276e549ff2f&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;704638493c12e4a309522ed487744229&quot;,
      &quot;document&quot;: &quot;39763465&quot;,
      &quot;kind&quot;: &quot;SENTENCE&quot;,
      &quot;start&quot;: 639,
      &quot;end&quot;: 748,
      &quot;tokens&quot;: 29,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;In combination, Shh and either Wnt-1 or Wnt-3 are sufficient to induce myogenesis in somitic tissue in vitro.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;0f572e2820ef9d83c4678562c93e7b9e&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;704638493c12e4a309522ed487744229&quot;,
      &quot;document&quot;: &quot;39763465&quot;,
      &quot;kind&quot;: &quot;SENTENCE&quot;,
      &quot;start&quot;: 749,
      &quot;end&quot;: 970,
      &quot;tokens&quot;: 52,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;Therefore, we propose that myotome formation in vivo may be directed by the combinatorial activity of Shh secreted by ventral midline tissues (floor plate and notochord) and Wnt ligands secreted by the dorsal neural tube.&quot;
    }
  ],

#### What V1 discarded / V2 recovered

<pre>{
  &quot;FIXED_SENTENCE_sentences_absent_in_V1&quot;: [
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;0a7e8081a354440f36a34d902fcdbd66&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;704638493c12e4a309522ed487744229&quot;,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;We have demonstrated previously that a combination of signals from the neural tube and the floor plate/notochord complex synergistically induce the expression of myogenic bHLH genes and myogenic differentiation markers in unspecified somites.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;0f572e2820ef9d83c4678562c93e7b9e&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;704638493c12e4a309522ed487744229&quot;,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;Therefore, we propose that myotome formation in vivo may be directed by the combinatorial activity of Shh secreted by ventral midline tissues (floor plate and notochord) and Wnt ligands secreted by the dorsal neural tube.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;148e798552d705ba6fae2ff15af08d68&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;2a3bd0d65fc4d8296105515162407ac2&quot;,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;Early in animal development, gradients of secreted morphogenic molecules, such as Sonic hedgehog (Shh), Wnt and TGFbeta/Bmp family members, regulate cell proliferation and determine the fate and phenotype of the target cells by activating well-characterized signalling pathways, which ultimately control gene transcription.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;1a83969da35277b2ac7caec4e7afb37d&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;366f4a2258eceed687ef5ce871fe6a16&quot;,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;Here, we show that this robust patterning depends on facilitated Chordin degradation and requires the expression of the Chordin-proteinase inhibitor Sizzled on the opposite side.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;21f8d20647bb94286ac774361f4356ed&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;366f4a2258eceed687ef5ce871fe6a16&quot;,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;Spemann&#x27;s organizer plays a key role in dorsal-ventral (DV) patterning in the amphibian embryo by secreting diffusible proteins such as Chordin, an antagonist to ventralizing bone morphogenetic proteins (BMPs).&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;2726f0a4d4dc4a2ceae6f2d4415554bc&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;704638493c12e4a309522ed487744229&quot;,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;In this study we demonstrate that Sonic hedgehog (Shh), which is expressed in the floor plate/notochord, and a subset of Wnt family members (Wnt-1, Wnt-3, and Wnt-4), which are expressed in dorsal regions of the neural tube, mimic the muscle inducing activity of these tissues.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;38cfcaa033ecca4af55fe4cd176bf919&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;344523a580470c759c23e14d113e57e4&quot;,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;The secreted polypeptide noggin mimics these activities and is expressed at the appropriate time and place to participate in the organizer signal.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;4cfd460a6cd2393122de4934c4b071b7&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;a6cfe1234925c8e8314e55e87e45ed63&quot;,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;In the Drosophila wing, a stripe of Notch activation maintains the dorsal-ventral compartment boundary, through a process that depends on the actin cytoskeleton.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;567317878b1a6be303ea116926dfc797&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;2be3b7dc6fe818970a8b7a0cc3a57f45&quot;,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;In this paper, we show that signals from the notochord pattern the expression of Pax-3, Pax-7 and Pax-9 in somites and the subsequent differentiation of cell types that arise from the somitic mesoderm.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;68dfcc7fae179b797d0b318f149c816c&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;deb12a411e8da4e6635a297d2f47aa2c&quot;,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;Dorsomorphin, unlike the endogenous BMP antagonist Noggin, robustly induces cardiomyogenesis when treatment is limited to the initial 24-hours of ES cell differentiation.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;6f83589d9448236c50dff567bac57407&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;a6cfe1234925c8e8314e55e87e45ed63&quot;,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;Here, we show that the dorsal-ventral boundary exhibits a distinct accumulation of Myosin II, and that this accumulation is regulated downstream of Notch signaling.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;733f9f9fb196cfd11c8c41e2fe1f6db4&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;344523a580470c759c23e14d113e57e4&quot;,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;Neural induction and mesoderm dorsalization are antagonized by bone morphogenetic proteins (BMPs), which induce epidermis and ventral mesoderm instead.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;75f1b77287230a31b7962ca60e400f2d&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;a6cfe1234925c8e8314e55e87e45ed63&quot;,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;These observations identify a distinct accumulation and requirement for Myosin activity in dorsal-ventral compartmentalization, and suggest a novel mechanism in which contractile tension along an F-actin cable at the compartment boundary contributes to compartmentalization.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;8331cb0b67287ef634cadb16f9db4d81&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;f4263525a6b0e458d98c7e682a769696&quot;,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;We discovered that quadruple knockdown of ADMP and BMP2/4/7 in Xenopus embryos eliminates self-regulation, causing ubiquitous neural induction throughout the ectoderm.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;8c5849a3113f95a77a26527d666bdb3b&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;deb12a411e8da4e6635a297d2f47aa2c&quot;,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;METHODOLOGY/ PRINCIPAL FINDINGS We describe the use of dorsomorphin, a selective small molecule inhibitor of BMP signaling, to induce myocardial differentiation in mouse ES cells.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;8e4ca0b533afa978d7abb4e578cfbebb&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;f4263525a6b0e458d98c7e682a769696&quot;,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;By transplanting dorsal or ventral wild-type grafts into ADMP/BMP2/4/7-depleted hosts, we demonstrate that both poles serve as signaling centers that can induce histotypic differentiation over considerable distances.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;a88e5db2d5a1d40c1b264869fcf7014d&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;f4263525a6b0e458d98c7e682a769696&quot;,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;Regulation of ADMP and BMP2/4/7 at Opposite Embryonic Poles Generates a Self-Regulating Morphogenetic Field&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;ae266fd30355fe786d72f3d633bb4f9d&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;deb12a411e8da4e6635a297d2f47aa2c&quot;,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;Dorsomorphin, a Selective Small Molecule Inhibitor of BMP Signaling, Promotes Cardiomyogenesis in Embryonic Stem Cells&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;cb251f4e015702d5e8f37abf511e80bc&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;2be3b7dc6fe818970a8b7a0cc3a57f45&quot;,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;These include Pax-3 and a closely related gene, Pax-7, both of which are expressed in the segmental plate and in the dermomyotome.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;d40df1c7434094f5f63ccad851c84f07&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;a6cfe1234925c8e8314e55e87e45ed63&quot;,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;We further show that mutations in the Myosin heavy chain subunit encoded by zipper can impair dorsal-ventral compartmentalization without affecting anterior-posterior compartmentalization.&quot;
    },
    {
      &quot;unit_id&quot;: &quot;de7f6aaa68f83bb988e16594e5091b90&quot;,
      &quot;parent&quot;: &quot;5c2b8121a72e9174430d2497cac148c2&quot;,
      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;In vertebrates, Notch activation has been shown to block MyoD activation and muscle differentiation in vitro, suggesting that this pathway may act to maintain the cells in an undifferentiated proliferative state.&quot;
    }
  ],

      &quot;text&quot;: &quot;This review discusses recent advances towards the understanding of this problem, showing how Shh, Wnt and TGFbeta/Bmp have adapted their &#x27;classical&#x27; signalling pathways or adopted alternative and novel molecular mechanisms to influence different aspects of neuronal circuit formation.&quot;
